scores.critic: Families are escort, isolated theft, isolated violence or unspecified wrongdoing, duty and betrayal, terminal repair, demands and shakedown, bare help requests, unconnected incidents and accepted requests, self-targeting request and reckoning, delivery, collection, gang-member removal, and refusal with social follow-up. Most fragments omit motives, concrete acts or usable subjects; naming a causal link rarely explains it. Requests to wrong the requester remain incoherent without further context. Resolved, protection and betrayal labels do not supply the missing outcomes. Paid jobs make actions clear but jump directly to completion, often withholding the discovery or consequence that would make following them rewarding. Timed repairs, escort needs and linked social responses offer the strongest everyday grounding. Repeated names, generic crimes and Kabuki labels alone provide little distinctive Night City texture.

The clearest families are paid errands, isolated wrongs, assault-driven help, duty-breaking discovery, and help that turns into a reckoning. Most traces omit concrete motives, requested acts and consequences; naming participants or declaring an outcome resolved does not supply those links. Requests to act against the asker are especially hard to interpret. The paid jobs offer useful objectives and plausible local concerns, but instant completion hides both the action and its payoff. Repeated structures with substituted names weaken individuality, while Night City often comes through only in gang references, eddies and a few locations. Explicit declines provide clearer resting points than unexplained closing labels.
